newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers mainly steady, Med quiet after flurr.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers mainly steady, Med quiet after flurr.

text.p: Dirty tanker rates were mainly steady on Thursday and the Mediterranean market paused for breath after a recent flurry of activity, brokers said.
Mideast/west very large crude carriers (VLCCs) were fixed at W55/52.5, while voyages to Japan were steady at about W67.5 and to Singapore at W60.
The West Africa/U.S. Gulf market was also little changed with VLCCs at W65 and five points higher to the U.K./Cont. West Africa/USG Suezmaxes (130,000 tonne vessels) were at an unchanged W95.
The Mediterranean Aframax (80,000 tonne) market, which was very busy on Wednesday, took a breather and dipped to W122.5 on lower enquiry, brokers said.
The inter-U.K./Cont Aframax sector was likewise quiet, with rates steady at W120.

The Caribs/upcoast sector, which tends to oscillate sharply, remained fairly flat as it has been for the last couple of weeks, but brokers said 70,000 tonne crude cargoes were slightly firmer at W172.5 after a long period at W170. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
